description: Replace the grouped block-256 batch-8 n=2048 path’s diagonal cuSOLVER calls with caller-stream batched MathDx/cuSolverDx 256x256 panel factorization. Launch one persistent CTA per matrix/panel frontier, reuse the existing grouped TRSM/rank-k schedule and shape cache, fuse factor copy/upper cleanup, and sweep tile/operator/workspace variants while preserving every other dispatch and full policy/correctness guards.

Replaced all eight grouped n=2048 diagonal SpotrfBatched calls with caller-current one-CTA-per-matrix MathDx factorization of each strided 256x256 panel, retaining the existing batched TRSM and strided-TF32 trailing updates. Build, policy gates, official validation, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed; target batch-8 n=2048 measured 2579.422 us and aggregate 963.772212 us versus the 970.669 us parent.

Widened the shared strided-panel MathDx operator from 64x64 to 128x128 tiles, reducing each 256 diagonal factorization to two stages while using about 192 KiB dynamic shared memory per CTA. All policy, correctness, fresh-input, and benchmark checks passed, but batch-8 n=2048 regressed from 2579.422 to 9871.546 us and the shared n256 cell regressed to 1126.288 us; aggregate measured 1187.661347 us.

Narrowed the shared strided-panel MathDx operator to 32x32 tiles, giving eight internal stages per 256 diagonal panel. All gates and benchmark correctness passed; batch-8 n=2048 improved from the 64-wide sample 2579.422 to 2537.074 us, while the shared n256 cell moved from 163.750 parent/177.777 trial-0 to 169.415 us. Full-grid aggregate measured 959.482380 us.

Separated n256 back to its selected 64-wide operator and reused the existing 32-wide n512 MathDx kernel for eight-tile n2048 panel factors by making its leading dimension and tile count dynamic. All checks passed and batch-8 n2048 retained 2541.037 us, but dynamic loop bounds regressed the preserved batch-640 n512 path from about 2.0 ms to 3082.840 us; aggregate measured 989.423974 us.

Specialized a separate constant-eight-stage 32x32 grouped-panel kernel so n256 retained its 64-wide operator and n512 regained its original constant-loop MathDx implementation. All validation passed; batch-640 n512 recovered from 3082.840 to 2017.429 us, batch-8 n2048 measured 2561.373 us, and aggregate was 964.370594 us. This isolates the grouped tile schedule without changing other MathDx operator widths.

Fused physical-lower cleanup into the final grouped diagonal MathDx CTA and returned the transposed view directly, removing the final full-tensor triu library pass. All policy and correctness checks passed, but only eight 128-thread CTAs performed the 2048-square cleanup, regressing the target from 2561.373 to 3003.089 us; aggregate measured 973.187495 us.

Restored the library cleanup and hoisted caller-current queue construction plus typed panel origins out of the eight-launch grouped MathDx loop. Every guard and benchmark cell passed. Batch-8 n=2048 improved from 2561.373 to 2500.987 us, n256 and n512 retained 165.988/1937.650 us samples, and aggregate reached 953.035972 us versus the 970.669 us parent.

Built one configured Numba launch object per grouped invocation and reused it for all eight typed panel origins, avoiding repeated grid/block/shared-memory indexing. Validation remained clean. The target measured 2526.312 us versus 2500.987 without configured-launch caching, and aggregate measured 956.117249 versus 953.035972, so this setup variant was slightly slower in the measured run.

Restored per-panel dispatch indexing and cached the external caller-queue wrapper across invocations by its current queue handle. All checks passed. Batch-8 n=2048 measured 2529.389 us versus 2500.987 for simple per-invocation queue hoisting and aggregate measured 957.307677 versus 953.035972, so persistent wrapper caching showed no measured gain.

Kept n256/n512 unchanged and gave only the grouped 32-wide panel kernel FP32-input/FP32-accumulate MathDx updates with four FP32 shared tiles (16 KiB), replacing its FP16 operand conversions. All checks passed, but batch-8 n=2048 regressed from 2500.987 to 2863.701 us and aggregate measured 972.204495 us; mixed FP16-input updates remained faster.

Restored mixed FP16 updates and tested a cached contiguous batch-8x256x256 factor workspace: each grouped diagonal was gathered from the strided n2048 output, factored in place by the selected 64-wide n256 MathDx operator, and scattered back before the unchanged TRSM/GEMM step. All checks passed; the target measured 2625.333 us versus 2500.987 for direct strided 32-wide panels, and aggregate was 963.414133 us.

Retained the contiguous grouped factor workspace but replaced its 64-wide factor with a dedicated constant-eight-stage 32x32 mixed MathDx operator. All checks passed. Batch-8 n=2048 improved from the packed-64 sample 2625.333 to 2504.541 us, statistically matching the direct-strided 32-wide 2500.987 sample despite two generic gather/scatter copies per panel; aggregate measured 955.820724 us.

Replaced generic strided workspace copies with dedicated caller-stream float4 pack/unpack kernels that transfer only the physical upper half of each 256 diagonal panel. Correctness and policy checks passed. The hosted benchmark sampled a uniform roughly 1.6x slowdown on every shape; target was 4064.257 us and aggregate 1565.333066 us, so this run does not isolate transfer cost from environment-wide variance.

Re-ran the vectorized upper-only pack/unpack design with cached outer panel origins after the prior environment-wide slow sample. All checks passed. The normal-speed run measured batch-8 n=2048 at 2574.282 us versus 2504.541 for generic full-panel copies and 2500.987 for direct strided panels; aggregate was 964.812423 us. The custom transfer launch did not recover its added setup cost.

Restored byte-identical direct-strided 32-wide grouped MathDx content after the packed-workspace and transfer variants. Final build, policy gates, official validation, fresh-input guard, and all benchmark cells passed. This repeat measured target 2614.896 us and aggregate 970.505203 us; the identical retained tree at d5adb76 measured the brief best 2500.987/953.035972 us, showing substantial hosted run variation.

Implemented caller-current MathDx diagonal factorization for every batch-8 n2048 grouped panel and retained best commit d5adb76a9944cecd84dda523c9a6348264283a7b: 953.035972 us aggregate and 2500.987 us on the target versus the 970.669 us parent and roughly 3.1 ms grouped-library target. The retained design uses a dedicated constant-eight-stage 32x32 FP16-input/FP32-accumulate factor kernel, preserves n256 64-wide and n512 constant-loop operators, hoists one caller queue wrapper across the eight launches, and leaves grouped TRSM/TF32 GEMM plus library cleanup unchanged. Direct 64/128-wide panels measured 2579.422/9871.546 us; dynamic shared dispatch preserved the target but regressed n512; fused eight-CTA cleanup measured 3003.089; configured-launch and persistent queue caching measured 2526.312/2529.389; FP32 updates measured 2863.701; packed 64/32-wide workspaces measured 2625.333/2504.541, and vectorized upper-only transfers reconfirmed at 2574.282. Final byte-identical build and all policy, official, fresh-input, and 15-cell checks pass; local profiling remained waived and hosted Brev unavailable. Keep the line moving with stage-specialized constant-origin panel entry points, a lower-overhead C++/driver bridge for the eight MathDx launches, or a cooperative multi-CTA diagonal wavefront that exposes more than eight resident CTAs without altering caller-stream ordering.
